purpose: Retain E rail removal effort, fragmented supports and local corner damage reported by the user.
status: Removable with greater effort than the usual rail supports; fragmented removal and local rough separation reported.

user_observations.verbatim: Well, that support was removable, though it certainly wasn't as easy as the rail supports, rail cavity supports normally are.

And I think that has more to do with the denser interface layer than anything else, that normally when they remove, like, it bends easier and the trees all come off as a single unit, but here it broke into several pieces, every tree or every couple of trees, and that's maybe just to be expected.

But still, it was a little bit difficult to remove, and I took a close-up photo there where you can see maybe that, like, right along the edge you get some lighter coloration from where it fused a bit there, and you can see from how it separated that it was not a clean separation, at least right on the corner there as I'm photographing it.
So in any case, I think I'd like to go with D for a while here, and both printers are now available.

visual_observations: The cavity underside retains parallel roads; a pale irregular strip is visible along the photographed corner.
interpretation_scope: The user attributes the stiffer fragmented mat mainly to interface density. Density and closer E contact are not independently isolated against the usual rail recipe by this result. Removal force and damaged area are unmeasured.
